summary: Stefano Zacchetti worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned degrees from Ca' Foscari University of Venice and studied at Sichuan and Leiden. He taught at Ca' Foscari, Soka University, and the University of Oxford from 2012 to 2020.

Steffen Döll specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology, earning his M.A. and doctorate at the University of Munich. He held posts at the University of Munich (2008–2015) and became Numata Professor of Japanese Buddhism at the University of Hamburg in 2015.

Steingrímur Bjarnason Thorsteinsson was an Icelandic scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Menntaskólinn í Reykjavík and the University of Copenhagen, later serving as a teacher (1872) and senior teacher (1895) at Menntaskólinn í Reykjavík.

Stella Kramrisch specialized in Indology and history/archaeology, receiving her Ph.D. from the University of Vienna. She held posts at Visva-Bharati, the University of Calcutta, the University of Pennsylvania (1950–1993), and the Philadelphia Museum of Art (1954–1972).
Stella Sandahl is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Armand Minard. She held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1984).

Sten Konow was an Indology, Iranian, and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Oslo and earned his Ph.D. under Richard Pischel at Halle. He held professorships at the University of Oslo and the University of Hamburg.

Stephan Licha works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After earning his PhD from SOAS University of London by 2012, he held postdoctoral positions at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo, later joining the faculty at the University of Chicago.
Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia, learning under Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephan V. Beyer is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Rochester and under Richard Hugh Robinson, later serving as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1972 to 1978.

Stephanie Kaza is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from Oberlin, Stanford, UC Santa Cruz, and Starr King. She served as an assistant professor and later Professor Emeritus (2005–2015) at the University of Vermont.
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar in the field of Tibetology. She completed her doctoral studies under the supervision of Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist and linguist who completed her doctorate at Yale under Stanley Insler and Warren Crawford Cowgill. She held posts at Harvard University and became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-Iranian Linguistics at UCLA in 2002.

Stephen Addiss was a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who studied at Harvard and the University of Michigan. He served as professor of art history at the University of Kansas and held a professorship at the University of Richmond.

Stephen Batchelor is an author and scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who trained at Songgwangsa and the Tibet Institute Rikon. He directed Sharpham College from circa 1992 to 2000 and joined Bodhi College as core faculty around 2015.

Stephen C. Berkwitz is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Vermont and earned his Ph.D. from UC Santa Barbara. He became an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Missouri State University in 1999.

Stephen F. Teiser works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Oberlin and Princeton, he joined Princeton University in 1988, where he became the D. T. Suzuki Professor in Buddhist Studies and Professor of Religion.

Stephen Fuchs worked in Indology and religious studies, completing his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna. He taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, visited the University of San Carlos, and became Director of the Institute of Indian Culture in 1967.

Stephen G. Covell is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his doctoral work at Princeton University under Jacqueline I. Stone and took up a post at Western Michigan University around 2001.
Stephen H. Phillips is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He served as a professor of philosophy and later professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin.
Stephen Harris is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of New Mexico by 2014 and became an Assistant Professor at Leiden University in 2014.
